title: /harden run profile (.harden/profile.json)
description: The owner's consent for an autonomous /harden run, written before the run (user-policy-autonomy U01-F04). In autonomous mode, the default, the run never waits for the user and answers every question from this file; a value the file lacks takes the conservative default named in its description, and the run logs that default (U01-F01). scripts/validate_profile.py is the authority: it applies this schema plus the checks a schema cannot express (a count_regex with exactly one capture group, a /regex/ that compiles and does not match the empty string, gate and e2e names unique across both lists, no gate or e2e command matching a forbidden pattern, cwd values that stay inside the repository). It also reports the 'blockers' that keep a valid profile report-only for anything that executes project code: mode report-only, live_side_effects not 'none', no gates, sandbox_ack false on native Windows, or a budget deadline already passed. With --repo it refuses a profile file that git tracks or the base commit holds, since that is repository text, never the owner's consent (protocol-preflight PF-22): an autonomous run then starts report-only with the reason 'profile is tracked by the repository; the owner's profile must be untracked'. Without an owner profile, an autonomous run writes one itself (self-setup: scripts/infer_profile.py, protocol-preflight step 6a, PF-23; user-policy-autonomy U01-F05), with 'origin' {kind: inferred} and a 'provenance' entry per field; the owner's /harden invocation is the consent. `run_state.py profile-template` drafts one for an owner who wants to write their own; assets/profile.example.json holds two complete profiles whose opt-ins carry their reasons.

comment.description: Free notes for the owner, such as the reason for each opt-in (assets/profile.example.json); ignored by the scripts.

template.description: Written by `run_state.py profile-template`. A profile that still carries this key is the unreviewed template and is invalid: the owner reviews every field, deletes the key and saves the file as .harden/profile.json. An agent never does this for the owner.

mode.description: auto (default): T0 and T1 are applied under this profile without asking. report-only: the run never edits. The live approvals of --interactive are chosen on the command line, not here.

gates.description: The project's own gate commands, in the format of .harden/config.json gates (gates.py --help). Default []: an autonomous run then executes no project code (protocol-preflight PF-20). verify_branch.py runs them from a fresh clone after the last fix, next to the gates of .harden/config.json.

e2e.description: End-to-end checks run by verify_branch.py from a fresh clone of the branch after the last fix (user-policy-autonomy U01-F02): the app boots, a CLI smoke run, a route probe, a golden capture (PF-16). Each must exit on its own; a non-zero exit code is a failure. Default []: the final verdict is 'gates only' (protocol-change PC-26).

network.description: Network scope of the run (skill-design T31-F15: network actions only on explicit request). registry-only allows lockfile installs (npm ci, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, uv sync --locked, cargo build --locked) and nothing else. With denied, verify_branch.py skips installs.

live_side_effects.description: none: the owner confirms that no gate, install or e2e command can reach live endpoints, keys, orders or chains (protocol-preflight PF-03). unconfirmed (default): no project code runs.

forbidden_commands.description: Commands the run must never execute (user-policy-autonomy U01-F03). A plain string matches as a case-insensitive substring of the command, whitespace runs folded to one space; the command is also tried with its quote characters removed. '/regex/' or '/regex/i' is a Python regular expression searched in the same forms. hook_guard.py refuses every Bash or PowerShell command that matches (reason_code profile-forbidden), and verify_branch.py refuses a check whose command matches. run_state.py start copies the list into .harden/active.

situation.description: The situation of prioritization.md step 3. Default: maintenance only. `run_state.py profile-template` leaves it empty (""), which is invalid, so the owner picks one or deletes the key to take the default.

future_work.description: Repository-relative paths or globs of the modules planned work will touch (prioritization.md step 3: they count as hot). Default []. For dead code the list is also the answer to the future-work question (lens-dead-code DC-17; pilot-auto-calibration A01-F17): code in a listed module that nothing calls yet stays work in progress, and while the list is empty or absent, code never referenced outside its file stays work in progress too, because the template pre-fills [].

auto_apply.description: Which T1 categories an autonomous run applies without asking. A switch the profile does not set reads as false; the profile template and a self-setup profile set every switch true except dependency_versions (the owner's decision of 2026-09-25, user-policy-autonomy U01-F06, U01-F08). owner_judgement lets the run decide, item by item, what the tier table leaves to the owner (T2, an additive public API change, a whole-repository format run) with prioritization.md's Owner-judgement lane: applied on the branch when a test or the change's own proof demonstrates it, the conservative option taken where two behaviours are valid, each commit listed under the report's Applied, review before merge. Never applied unattended, whatever these say: a change on a live-effect path (key material, signing, order or transaction submission, deploys, emulated chain system contracts), secrets, CI and gate configs, history, a package no manifest lists, a new suppression, a breaking change a consumer outside the repository sees, test deletions and removals or changes of existing test lines (checked additions are applied, U01-F07) (U01-F03, U01-F12).

dependency_versions.description: true also approves a dependency change that adds or changes a resolved version in a lockfile (DP-08, DP-09, DP-10, SE-21), which also needs 'dependencies'. Self-setup never sets it (user-policy-autonomy U01-F08): with 'dependencies' alone, only changes whose lockfile diff adds no resolved version are applied. Before 2026-09-25, `dependencies` alone approved these items; an owner profile must now set both. Under `network: registry-only` a change that fetches a version the lockfile does not hold is already outside the network scope, so this switch mostly covers offline re-resolutions (DP-08). Even with it, a version the base lockfile does not hold stays report-only while a secret file sits in the repository or a directory above it (U01-F12).

money_paths_globs.description: Which files are on a money, order, key, signing or transaction path (pilot-auto-calibration A01-F06 to A01-F08). Absent (the default): the lens and verifier judgement decides, and a disagreement takes the reading that withholds. Present, even empty: a file is on a money path when its repository-relative path, or a directory above it, matches a pattern, and otherwise it is not, except code that signs, sends orders or transactions, or handles keys, which the run keeps on a money path whatever the list says. auto_apply.money_paths approves the items on those paths; the list approves nothing. Dialect: the .gitignore pattern format without '!' negation, backslash escapes or comments; '*', '?' and '[...]' stay inside one path segment, '**' is a whole segment, a pattern without '/' (other than a trailing one) matches a name at any depth, a trailing '/' matches a directory, never a file; '[[]' matches a literal '[', and a negated class '[!...]' may also match '/', which only widens the list; letter case is ignored on every platform. No leading '/', drive letter, '.' or '..' segment, or backslash. A pattern that matches no tracked file makes the run ignore the whole list until it matches one. `validate_profile.py PATH --repo DIR --classify [FILE ...]` prints the verdict for each file.

origin.description: Who wrote this profile. Absent or kind 'owner': the owner's file (user-policy-autonomy U01-F04). Kind 'inferred': written by scripts/infer_profile.py during self-setup (protocol-preflight step 6a, PF-23); the owner's /harden invocation is the consent (U01-F05). Self-setup replaces an inferred profile on the next run; an owner who edits one sets kind to 'owner' (or deletes origin) to keep it.

provenance.description: Where each field's value came from: a tracked file and line, a rule, the platform, an owner decision, the pre-start probe or the review (protocol-preflight PF-23). Keys: mode, network, live_side_effects, sandbox_ack, situation, future_work, budget, env, install, auto_apply.<switch>, gates.<name>, e2e.<name>, forbidden_commands[<i>], money_paths_globs[<i>]. A key may describe a field the profile leaves out (why it took its default). Ignored by every decision; run_state.py start copies it into .harden/progress.md and the report shows it.

sandbox_ack.description: true: the owner accepts that project code runs without a Claude Code sandbox (native Windows has none) or in bypassPermissions mode (protocol-preflight PF-03). Default false, which keeps such a run report-only.

budget.description: Optional limits. A deadline already passed at run start keeps the run report-only; verify_branch.py always finishes its loop, whatever the deadline. The run's deadline is the earlier of deadline_utc and start + max_minutes; without either, budget.py sizes it on the in-scope LOC (60 min + 20 per 1,000 LOC, 120 to 600). max_usd, when set, caps the spend at list prices measured from the session and subagent transcripts; without it spend is measured and reported, never enforced. max_tokens is the detection token cap of the ledger (detection DT-25). pilot-auto-calibration A01-F34.

detection.description: How detection runs (pilot-auto-calibration A01-F33, A01-F35, A01-F36): at most max_concurrent_subagents subagents at once (default 4); lens_bundles auto lets budget.py plan choose one lens per pass or bundles of at most three; pass_model, when set, is passed as the Agent tool's model for every lens pass (unset: the agent definition's model). The ledger records the model each pass actually ran on.

cmd.description: A string runs through the platform shell (cmd.exe on Windows, /bin/sh elsewhere); a list runs as argv without a shell.

cwd.description: Relative to the repository root (and so to each fresh clone); never absolute, never '..'.

count_regex.description: Exactly one capture group, except with count_mode matches (gates.py --help).

ratchet.description: A no-new-violations gate judged by its count against the base (PF-11); needs count_regex.

compare.description: true: verify_branch.py also runs the check on a clone of the base, and the two stdouts must match once ANSI codes, ISO 8601 timestamps, clock times, durations (12ms, 1.5 s, 3 seconds) and the clone's path are masked.
